description:
New workspace-member crate crates/outram-fmt with a [[bin]] 'outram-fmt'. Responsibilities:
1. Run 'cargo fmt --all' (rustfmt, honoring root rustfmt.toml max_width=80).
2. Run 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release' (per release-mode rule) and surface warnings; support treating warnings as errors in --check mode.
3. Line-length checker: scan all tracked *.rs (skip target/, vendor/, generated files), report every line >80 chars with file:line, and fail (non-zero exit) in --check mode.
Modes: default = do the pass (fmt in place, clippy report, line report); --check = non-mutating gate for CI/pre-commit (fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, line-length hard-fail).
Design constraints (workspace rules apply): std-only where possible so it still compiles for Android (host tool, but must not break 'cargo check --workspace'); no trait objects (enum dispatch), no Box<T>, no lifetime params; doc-comment every public item; //! module docs. Uses std::process::Command to shell out to cargo.
Depends on the rustfmt.toml bead (consumes that config).
title: Build the outram-fmt Rust binary (fmt + clippy + 80-char checker)

description:
Found by the full workspace test run 2026-08-04. Test: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference. Suite otherwise green (163 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored).

ERROR:
  wgpu error: Validation Error
   In Device::create_bind_group_layout, label = 'surf_dist.bgl'
     Too many bindings of type StorageBuffers in Stage ShaderStages(COMPUTE),
     limit is 4, count was 7. Check the limit max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage
     passed to Adapter::request_device

SITE: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/gpu/surface_distance.rs:861 (the 'surf_dist.bgl' layout).

NOT AN ENVIRONMENT PROBLEM: other GPU tests in this same crate pass on this machine (gpu::batched_flight::tests::gpu_lcg_state_matches_cpu, gpu::xs_interp::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference, gpu::union_grid::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_native_union), so an adapter is present and working. This layout specifically asks for more storage buffers than the device was granted.

TWO FIXES, DIFFERENT CONSEQUENCES -- pick deliberately:
  (a) Request a higher max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage when creating the device. Works if the hardware supports it, but silently narrows which GPUs can run this kernel, and wgpu's downlevel/WebGL tier caps this at 4. Check what limits Adapter::request_device is currently called with -- if it is using defaults, that is likely the whole story.
  (b) Pack the 7 storage buffers into 4 or fewer (combine into a single buffer with offsets, or move read-only data into a uniform/storage-texture). Portable across every adapter tier, more work.

Note the CPU path is the trusted/deterministic reference in this workspace and GPU is acceleration only, so this does not affect correctness of results -- but the test is genuinely failing and the GPU surface-distance path is unusable on any adapter with a 4-buffer limit.

Deferred by the maintainer 2026-08-04 (the sibling boon-lay WGSL reserved-keyword failure was fixed immediately in the same session).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, 2026-08-06.

The limit was self-imposed, not hardware. src/gpu/mod.rs probe() requested wgpu::Limits::downlevel_defaults(), which pins max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage to 4. surf_dist.bgl binds 7 storage buffers (bindings 0-5 and 7; binding 6 is a uniform), so create_bind_group_layout rejected it.

What the hardware actually reports on this machine (sourced at runtime, not assumed):
  adapter                              NVIDIA RTX A5000 (NVK GA102), Vulkan, Discrete
  max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage 524288   (wgpu's view; vulkaninfo maxPerStageDescriptorStorageBuffers reports 1048576 -- wgpu applies its own cap)
  max_storage_buffer_binding_size      2147483644
  max_buffer_size                      2147483648
  max_compute_invocations_per_workgroup 1024
  max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension  65535
  cpu_threads                          32 (i9-13900K, 24C/32T)

So we were asking for 7 against a self-imposed ceiling of 4 on a device that allows 524288.

FIX: probe() now requests adapter.limits() -- always satisfiable by definition, so it cannot fail where the old call succeeded. GpuContext gained a  field carrying the sourced GpuLimits.

NEW MODULE src/gpu/capabilities.rs (12 tests, all passing, builds on Android since it holds no wgpu types):
  - GpuLimits / DeviceClass / HardwareCapabilities -- limits read from adapter.limits() + get_info(), CPU threads from available_parallelism()
  - supports_storage_buffers(n) -- ask BEFORE building a layout; a device that genuinely cannot host the kernel now falls back to CPU instead of panicking
  - max_chunk_items(stride, workgroup_size) -- dispatch chunking from binding-size AND workgroup-count limits (4194240 queries here)
  - plan_split(...) -> WorkSplit with a SplitReason, guaranteeing gpu_items + cpu_items == total

HYBRID PATH: surface_distance_hybrid() splits a batch across both devices -- CPU half on a rayon parallel iterator inside a scoped thread while this thread drives the GPU dispatch, so they genuinely overlap. Auto policy gives a discrete GPU 0.75 and the CPU 0.25 (integrated 0.5/0.5; software adapter 0.0 since it IS the cpu). Those Auto constants are device-class heuristics, NOT measurements -- measured_gpu_fraction(gpu_rate, cpu_rate) is provided to compute the real ratio from a benchmark and feed it back as SplitPolicy::GpuFraction.

NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD YET: gpu_matches_cpu_reference still fails, but for a DIFFERENT and newly-visible reason -- the GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with the CPU mirror. Filed separately. This bead's specific defect (bind group exceeds the limit) is resolved; close it when you are satisfied that separation is right.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Correction to the previous comment: two fragments were eaten by shell backtick expansion when it was posted.

1. "GpuContext gained a  field" should read: GpuContext gained a "limits" field carrying the sourced GpuLimits, plus a capabilities() method returning HardwareCapabilities.

2. A dropped bullet from the capabilities.rs list:
   - supports_storage_buffers(n) -- ask BEFORE building a bind group layout. A device that genuinely cannot host the kernel now yields an all-CPU WorkSplit with reason InsufficientStorageBuffers instead of panicking. That is the guard that would have turned the original op-bjd panic into a clean fallback on a limited machine.

3. The separately-filed bug is op-9s8.11 (GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with CPU mirror).

Test state after the fix: 196 passed, 1 failed, 3 ignored. The single failure is gpu_matches_cpu_reference, failing on the torus disagreement (op-9s8.11), NOT on bind-group limits.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: RESOLVED AND VERIFIED GREEN, 2026-08-06. The blocking defect op-9s8.11 (and op-9s8.12 alongside it) is fixed, so gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference now PASSES over all 19440 queries and all 15 surface types on the RTX A5000. Full crate suite: 199 passed, 0 failed. The bind-group-limit defect this bead was filed for was fixed earlier by sourcing adapter.limits() instead of Limits::downlevel_defaults(); the test it guards is now green too, so there is nothing left separating the two. Closing.

title: outram-mc-libs: surf_dist bind group exceeds max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage (GPU test fails)

description:
ACTION: a human must verify these citations against the actual books before any of them appears in a publication, an arXiv draft, or anywhere the project asserts provenance.

WHAT HAPPENED. On 2026-08-11 an AI assistant supplied the literature basis for the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discretization used to replace the growing response vectors in chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator (bead op-fm5), and for the analytic exponential integration in crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs. The citations were produced FROM MODEL KNOWLEDGE while offline. Authors, titles and publishers are asserted with reasonable confidence. EDITIONS, YEARS, PAGE NUMBERS, CHAPTER NUMBERS AND EQUATION NUMBERS WERE NOT VERIFIED AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED CORRECT.

This is exactly the failure mode RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md exists to prevent, and exactly the class of error AI_USAGE.md requires a human to catch. A plausible-looking but wrong citation is worse than no citation, because it survives review by looking right.

CITATIONS TO CHECK:

Sampled-data control theory (the primary basis - the discretization is EXACT, not an approximation, for piecewise-constant input):
1. Astrom, K. J. and Wittenmark, B., "Computer-Controlled Systems: Theory and Design", Prentice Hall. Claimed to derive x[k+1] = Phi x[k] + Gamma u[k] with Phi = exp(A*T) and Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A*s) ds * B in its sampling-of-continuous-systems chapter. VERIFY the chapter and that the result is stated as exact.
2. Seborg, D. E., Edgar, T. F., Mellichamp, D. A. and Doyle, F. J., "Process Dynamics and Control", Wiley.
3. Franklin, G. F., Powell, J. D. and Workman, M. L., "Digital Control of Dynamic Systems", Addison-Wesley.
4. Ogata, K., "Discrete-Time Control Systems", Prentice Hall.

Numerical ODE framing (used in decay_heat.rs, where the motivation is stiffness rather than sampling):
5. Hochbruck, M. and Ostermann, A., "Exponential integrators", Acta Numerica, volume 19 (2010), pages 209-286. The volume, year and page range are asserted and SHOULD BE CHECKED - a journal citation with a specific page range is the easiest of these to get wrong and the easiest to verify.

Signal-processing framing (one-pole IIR filter via impulse invariance):
6. Oppenheim, A. V. and Schafer, R. W., "Discrete-Time Signal Processing", Prentice Hall.
7. Smith, J. O. III, "Introduction to Digital Filters", W3K Publishing. Claimed to be freely available from Stanford CCRMA. If true this is the only OPEN-ACCESS item in the list and the one to prefer where a paywall-free citation is wanted - VERIFY the free availability and the exact title, which has appeared with an "with Audio Applications" subtitle.

ACCESS TIER. Items 1-6 are commercial textbooks and one paywalled journal - proprietary under DATA_POLICY.md. Do NOT ingest them into crates/kovan-literature/open/. The mathematical results are textbook-standard and freely implementable; only the publications are gated. Item 7, if the free availability checks out, may be catalogued open.

ACCEPTANCE: each citation either confirmed with its verified edition/year/pages recorded in the doc comment, or corrected, or removed. Until that is done, every doc comment carrying one of these must retain its unverified-citation disclaimer.
title: VERIFY CITATIONS: textbook references for the O(1) / ZOH recurrence were supplied from model knowledge, not checked
